title: Lightweight Explainable Physics-Informed Neural Networks by Learnable Activation Function
content: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) provide a data-efficient framework for solving partial differential equations, but improving their accuracy often requires enlarging multilayer perceptron (MLP) backbones, increasing parameter count and computational cost. This study investigates whether PINN performance can be improved while keeping the underlying network lightweight. We introduce two new learnable activation functions for compact PINNs: (1) the Cannistraci-Muscoloni-Gu Generalized Logistic-Logit Function (CMG-GLLF) and (2) CMG-GELU, which replaces the tanh term in the GELU approximation with learnable CMG. The generalized logistic-logit function enables learnable, adaptive feature announcement and suppression, defining the nonlinear feature transformation used by the trained network. To make CMG practical for PINN training, we reformulate its implicit logit-phase approximation into an explicit differentiable form using a one-step Newton approximation, reducing numerical instability and computational overhead. Empirical validation on Burgers' equation shows that the explicit CMG formulation substantially outperforms both the implicit CMG implementation and fixed tanh activation, which is widely used as a PINN nonlinearity. We further show that a layer-wise CMG design achieves a favorable accuracy-parameter trade-off, adding only two trainable parameters per hidden layer while improving over Vanilla MLPs across the benchmark suite. After selecting the layer-wise CMG-Explicit strategy, we compare layer-wise CMG and CMG-GELU with recent state-of-the-art PINN methods, including new network architectures, adaptive and static activation functions, contextual modulation, and Vanilla MLP with tanh activation, across 20 PINN tasks spanning multiple dimensions and physical phenomena. With 20 tasks, our evaluation covers substantially more benchmark tasks than the recent method papers. By ranking methods within each task according to their performance, we calculate mean rank and the Robustness Performance Ranking Index (RPRI), which favors low mean rank and low rank variation across tasks. Among the 12 compared methods, CMG-GELU, proposed here for the first time, achieves the best mean rank, the lowest rank SD, and the best overall RPRI, while CMG ranks second by RPRI. We further analyze CMG and CMG-GELU parameters across tasks and hidden layers, revealing distinct learned announcement/suppression patterns and providing parameter-level explainability by showing where the trained network applies relatively stronger feature announcement or suppression. These results suggest that learnable activation functions offer a practical route toward lightweight, accurate, and explainable PINNs.
